sources.entry: BinPastes - Minimal pastebin supporting client-side encryption, fulltext search, one-time messages. Intended for one to few users looking for a simple pastebin deployment. Apache-2.0 Java

summary.one_liner: BinPastes is a minimal self-hosted pastebin written in Java that supports client-side encryption, full-text search, and expiring notes.
summary.what_it_does: The README lists an overview of notes with full-text search, and notes that can expire after a set time or never expire. Each note's visibility can be adjusted. Content can be encrypted client-side. A dark mode is included. It is packaged as a single JDK-run jar, and it requires MySQL 8+ as its database for production use. The README describes it as a simple deployment, and the awesome-selfhosted listing says it is aimed at one to a few users. The README does not describe one-time messages, though the listing mentions them.
use_cases: self-hosted pastebin for a small team
sharing code snippets or notes with expiry
how_to_run: Copy application-mysql.properties next to binpastes.jar and set mysql.host, mysql.database, mysql.username, mysql.password
notable: Configurable note expiry, including never expire
Single runnable jar with no separate build tooling needed to run
caveats: Requires a MySQL 8+ database for productive use
README gives no detail on one-time messages despite the listing mentioning them
